nodes.label: Discovery: two separate concerns
nodes.rationale: Seed providers answer 'which addresses do I try at join time' and run once; the Receptionist answers 'which actors are registered under this service key' and runs continuously. They share the name because both are lookup-based addressing, but the protocols and use cases differ. Framework discovery is cluster-internal — external service discovery stays your infrastructure's job.

nodes.label: Seed provider
nodes.rationale: Four ship: ConfigSeedProvider (static list), DnsSeedProvider (SRV/A records), KubernetesApiSeedProvider (live pod listing) and AggregateSeedProvider (chained with fallback). Pick by deployment environment and move on.

nodes.label: A lookup is not yet an answer
nodes.rationale: A provider returns what it sees right now, which during a simultaneous start differs per node — DNS mid-propagation, a pod Ready before its IP is published, a paginated incomplete API listing — so a node joining on the first answer forms a cluster from its own partial view. Cluster Bootstrap wraps any provider: it polls until the returned set stops changing, then lets exactly one node form the cluster. It is a phase above the providers, not a replacement.
